To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lattice constant of Al-doped Mg2Sil can be increased by the substitution of Al for Si, Mg, or the interstitial site, while the lattice constant of Sb-doped MgSi can be reduced by the substitution of Sb for Si; Al tends to substitute for Mg at a higher concentration (>4 at.%), while Sb tends to substitute for Si at all concentrations; the Seebeck coefficient of Al-doped (Sb-doped) MgSi is enhanced (reduced) by increasing
the lattice constant and the Seebeck coefficient can be affected by doping impurity atoms into Mg2Si.

the insertion of Al or Sb impurities into Mg2Si can lead to the formation of various types of defect states in the band structure, and that these defect states can be responsible for the observed Seebeck coefficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Al and Sb impurity doping on the thermoelectric properties.
the structural and thermomechanical properties of Al- and/or Sb-doped MgSi, which are expected to play an important role as a thermoelectric material in the future.
the effects of impurity atoms on the structural and thermodynamic properties of the Mg2Si system, which is expected to be a promising candidate material for thermoelectric devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although both Al and Sb impurities can enhance the power factor of Mg2Si, the former is more effective than the latter.

the thermoelectric properties are affected by the site occupation of the impurity elements, and the Seebeck coefficient is enhanced by Al doping, while the thermal conductivity is suppressed by both Al and Sb doping.
the Al- and the Sb-doped Mg 2 Si systems show an enhancement in Seebeck coefficients, which is a key property in the thermoelectric materials, as compared to that of the undoped Mg2Si system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Al doping is effective for improving the Seebeck coefficient, but not for the electrical conductivity, whereas Sb doping is effective for both the Seebeck coefficient and the electrical conductivity.

the Al- and/or Sb-doping of Mg2Si is expected to improve the Seebeck coefficient and thus the thermoelectric efficiency, while the lattice constant and the formation energy of the doped system can be tuned by adjusting the doping concentration.
the Al-doped system has a high Seebeck coefficient and the Sb-doped system has low lattice thermal conductivity, which are the two important parameters in the thermoelectric figure of merit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Seebeck coefficient is significantly affected by the site occupation of impurities in Mg2Si.
, in contrast to Al doping, Sb doping can lead to a higher thermoelectromagnetic force, and hence a better thermoelectric figure-of-merit, in Mg2Si.
the Seebeck coefficient can be enhanced by the impurities at a low doping level (2-4 at.%), which is a promising result for thermoelectric applications.
